answer_part: The control device formulation employs ODADI at 0.5 mg/mL as a surface passivation layer, which contributes to performance enhancement but exhibits limitations in mitigating interfacial recombination and ionic defects. Analysis reveals that ODADI, while beneficial for initial interface refinement, inadequately suppresses deep-level trap states at the perovskite surface due to suboptimal molecular conformation and binding affinity with undercoordinated lead ions. This results in persistent non-radiative recombination losses, evident from the moderate open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.13971 V and fill factor (FF) of 81.564%, indicating significant voltage and charge extraction deficits. The current density (Jsc) of 25.6893 mA/cm² remains robust but is constrained by residual surface defects that limit carrier lifetime. PDADI, a structural analog with para-substituted aromatic functionality, offers superior passivation through enhanced steric hindrance and stronger Lewis base coordination with Pb²⁺ sites. This modification directly addresses the failure mode of incomplete surface defect passivation in the control device, reducing trap-assisted recombination and suppressing ion migration at the perovskite/hole-transport interface. Consequently, Voc increases due to diminished Shockley-Read-Hall recombination, while FF improves from reduced series resistance and more efficient charge extraction. A minor trade-off involves a marginal Jsc reduction from potential light absorption competition by the passivator layer, but this is outweighed by the substantial gains in voltage and fill factor. The optimized formulation replaces ODADI with PDADI at 0.5 mg/mL in the passivation solution, maintaining all other compositional elements—including the perovskite precursor (Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ at 1.65 mol/L), SAM (4,4,4-NA at 0.5 mg/mL), and additives (MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL)—unchanged to isolate the passivator effect. This adjustment elevates device metrics to a Voc range of 1.17–1.20 V, Jsc of 25.4–25.8 mA/cm², FF of 83.9–85.9%, and power conversion efficiency of 24.8–26.6%, reflecting significant suppression of interfacial recombination without altering processing parameters.
control_device_fabrication: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.8806% under an active area of 0.09 cm², with a VOC value of 1.13971 V, an FF value of 81.564%, and a current density (JSC) of 25.6893 mA/cm². The perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3) precursor solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.65 mol/L in a mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. Incorporating 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) as a SAM was critical to adjust interfacial energy levels and refine the perovskite interface. The controlled addition of MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) additives were implemented. The precursor solution was spin-coated on substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the last step, 150 µL of CB was dropped on the film at 15 s. An annealing process at 110 °C for 15 min allowed the perovskite grains to fully mature. The application of ODADI (0.5 mg/mL) as a passivation layer via spin-coating significantly boosted device performance. The passivation layers were sequentially spin-coated on the perovskite surface at 5000 rpm for 30 s. To improve passivation, 70 µL of passivator was dropped at 6 s during spin-coating. It was then annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min to remove the solvent residual. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: The control device displays a JSC of 25.5903 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1862 V and an FF of 84.8668%, turning out a moderate PCE of 25.7614%. In formulating the active solution, Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 at 1.65 mol/L was utilized to establish the perovskite layer. A SAM solution consisting of 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) in ethanol was prepared. In addition, MACl (15.0 mg/mL), and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL, 520 mg mL-1 in acetonitrile) were incorporated to improve its conductivity. The precursor solution was spin-coated in a two-step process at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. 150 µL of antisolvent was drop-coated onto the substrate at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. The perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min. To optimize device performance, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was uniformly spin-coated onto the perovskite surface to form an effective passivation layer. For the passivation layer, spin-coating parameters were 5000 rpm and 30 s. At 6 s, a drop of 70 µL passivator was introduced during spin-coating. Thermal treatment involved annealing at 100 °C for 5 min to facilitate crystallization. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
